jobs.change: the GRIP: change it to an UNDERHAND (supinated) chin-up grip — palms facing the athlete's own face (toward the camera side), fingers wrapping over the bar from the camera side, thumbs pointing outward to the sides; hands exactly shoulder-width apart (narrower than now, directly above the shoulders), so the upper arms run almost parallel

the GRIP: change it to an UNDERHAND (supinated) chin-up grip — palms facing the athlete's own face (toward the camera side), fingers wrapping over the bar from the camera side; hands exactly shoulder-width apart, arms straight in a dead hang

the feet and ankles: the athlete rises HIGH onto the balls of the feet on the step edge — heels lifted about 8 cm above the step, ankles fully extended (plantar-flexed), knees straight, calves contracted and glowing brightest
the feet and ankles: only the balls of the feet on the step edge, heels LOWERED BELOW the step edge (about 5 cm under its top surface), calves stretched, knees straight, body otherwise unchanged

the shoulders: shrugged straight UP toward the ears as high as possible (about 5 cm higher than now), arms still straight, the dumbbells rise by the same amount; the upper trapezius bulges and glows brightest; neck neutral
the REAR foot: its top (instep) rests firmly ON the bench pad with no gap — the foot touches and slightly presses into the pad; everything else unchanged
the head: chin slightly tucked, gaze forward along the thighs toward the knees (not tipped back); everything else unchanged

the arms and head: elbows bent about 90° with the FOREARMS VERTICAL (hands flat on the floor under the elbows, forearms NOT lying on the floor), the top of the head lowered to just above the floor slightly in front of the hands, hips still high in an inverted V

the band: remove the rigid lime-green rod across the back. Instead the athlete holds a thin DARK-GREY elastic resistance band; the band runs IN FRONT of the chest between the two hands (so from behind only its two ends near the hands are visible), arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height. The band must not glow

the dumbbells: each dumbbell handle runs ACROSS the palm, perpendicular to the forearm (seen end-on from the front exactly like the dumbbells in image 2), knuckles up, pinky side slightly higher; arms and everything else unchanged

the arms: press the barbell to FULL LOCKOUT — arms completely straight overhead, elbows locked, the bar directly above the middle of the feet and slightly behind the forehead, head pushed slightly forward through the arms; body upright, glutes and core braced

the start of the press: the barbell RESTING ON THE FRONT SHOULDERS at collarbone height (touching the front deltoids, NOT at the chin or face), forearms vertical, elbows slightly in front of the bar, hands just outside shoulder width, head straight
the glow: remove the lime glow from the shoulders, biceps and forearms (they become natural deep red); keep the glow on the thighs and glutes exactly as it is
the glow: remove the lime glow from the shoulders, biceps and forearms (they become natural deep red); keep the glow on the thighs and glutes exactly as it is
the glow: remove the lime glow from the SUPPORTING arm that rests on the bench (it becomes natural deep red); keep the glow on the back and the working arm's rear shoulder exactly as it is
the glow: remove the lime glow from the SUPPORTING arm that rests on the bench (it becomes natural deep red); keep the glow on the back exactly as it is
the bar position: lower the barbell so it TOUCHES the upper chest just below the collarbones, forearms vertical under the bar, elbows about 60° from the torso
the arms: make them SYMMETRIC — both arms open wide to the sides at shoulder height, elbows slightly bent, each forearm/hand on its machine handle or pad, chest stretched; both arms mirror each other

the knee pads and bar: BOTH thighs are locked under a pair of padded rollers directly on top of the thighs just above the knees; the bar is pulled down to the UPPER CHEST (just below the collarbones), not the chin
the knee pads: BOTH thighs are locked under a pair of padded rollers directly on top of the thighs just above the knees; everything else unchanged

Camera: FRONT THREE-QUARTER view — 35° in front of the athlete's right side, at hip height, so the face, the bar on the front of the shoulders and the high elbows are all clearly visible; the plates must NOT hide the head. Front-rack: bar resting on the front deltoids against the collarbones, fingertips under the bar, elbows high and pointing forward, torso nearly upright, thighs parallel to the floor, heels flat.

Camera: front three-quarter view from the athlete's right at bench height, so the barbell runs INTO the depth of the image (seen at an angle, not parallel to the body). A barbell fixed in a power rack at hip height. The athlete hangs under it, body straight from head to heels, heels on the floor, both hands gripping the bar shoulder-width with an overhand grip, arms bent, CHEST TOUCHING the bar at the top, shoulder blades squeezed together. Glow on lats, mid-traps, rhomboids and rear delts.

Camera: side view from the athlete's right at floor level. Bottom of a push-up: palms FLAT on the floor directly under the lower chest, slightly wider than shoulders, forearms VERTICAL, elbows about 45° from the torso, chest 3 cm above the floor, body one straight line from head to heels, no equipment at all.

Camera: high three-quarter view from above the athlete's right side. Lying on the back on the floor, lower back pressed flat. The athlete's RIGHT arm is extended back overhead, hovering just above the floor; the LEFT leg is extended straight, hovering just above the floor. The LEFT arm points straight up to the ceiling and the RIGHT knee is bent 90° directly above the hip (thigh vertical, shin horizontal). Opposite arm and leg are extended — never the same side.

Camera: side view from the athlete's right at hip height. The athlete kneels FACING the cable column (the weight stack in front of him), holding a rope attachment from the HIGH pulley with both hands beside the head. Contracted position: spine flexed and curled down, ribs pulled toward the pelvis, elbows down near the mid-thighs, hips stay above the knees (they do not sit back).

A real plate-loaded HACK SQUAT machine: an inclined back-pad sled (45°) that slides on two rails, with shoulder pads attached to the top of the same sled, and an angled foot platform at the bottom. Bottom position: the athlete's ENTIRE BACK, from hips to shoulders, is pressed flat against the inclined back pad, shoulders under the shoulder pads, hands on the side handles, both feet flat on the angled platform shoulder-width, thighs parallel to the platform. Camera: side view from the athlete's right.

A seated LEG EXTENSION machine: the athlete's knees are exactly in line with the machine's pivot axis (a round cam at the front edge of the seat, right beside the knee joint); a lever arm runs from that pivot down to a padded roller resting on the front of the lower shins just above the ankles. Back against the backrest, hands gripping the side handles by the seat. Top position: legs straight out in front, the lever arm and roller lifted with them. Camera: side view from the athlete's right.

A SEATED LEG CURL machine: back against the backrest, a thigh pad clamping the thighs from above, knees in line with the machine's pivot axis at the front edge of the seat; a lever arm from the pivot to a padded roller BEHIND the lower calves at the Achilles tendon. Contracted position: knees bent about 90°, the roller pushed down and back under the seat. Hands on the side handles. Camera: side view from the athlete's right.

A seated CHEST PRESS machine: two handles on lever arms that are clearly attached to the machine frame and pivot (no floating handles); the weight stack is BEHIND the athlete, not in front. Start position: back flat on the upright back pad, handles at mid-chest height beside the chest, elbows about 60° from the torso, forearms horizontal and in line with the handles, feet flat on the floor. Camera: front three-quarter view from the athlete's right.

A seated SHOULDER PRESS machine: two handles on press arms that are clearly attached to the machine frame (no floating handles). Start position: back against the upright pad, handles beside the head at shoulder level, forearms vertical under the handles, elbows below the hands and slightly forward. Camera: front three-quarter view from the athlete's right.

standing tall at lockout, the barbell hanging in straight arms against the thighs. Keep the SAME camera, framing and SCALE as image 1 — the athlete must appear the same size
standing tall at the top, the dumbbells hanging in straight arms IN FRONT OF THE THIGHS with the SAME overhand grip as image 1 (dumbbells across the front of the thighs, not at the sides)
standing tall at the top, the bar still on the upper back inside the guide rails; the Smith machine frame stays exactly as in image 1 with its uprights standing on the floor
legs pushed out almost straight (knees slightly bent, not locked); the footplate AND the weight horns with the plates move together as one sled along the rails; back still flat on the pad
